newsitem.title: FRANCE: France plans to extend textiles aid, plea to EU.
newsitem.headline: France plans to extend textiles aid, plea to EU.

text.p: French Labour Minister Jacques Barrot said on Tuesday he planned to extend a state aid scheme used to stem job losses in the textiles sector and hoped that the European Commission would not ban the existing scheme at a meeting in Brussels on Wednesday.

He told a news conference the existing scheme, which offers subsidies in the form of relief on payroll charges for textiles employers, would be extended and said France was working with the Commission to make it conform with European Union law.

European Commissioner Karel Van Miert, who has powers to vet subsidies to ensure fair competition within the EU, agreed to much of the scheme but wanted it applied on a company-by-company basis rather than as a sector-wide programme, Barrot said.
"I hope this last final plea will be heard," Barrot said.

He said he hoped the Commission would put off a decision or, at least, that any warning from Van Miert on Wednesday would be accompanied by a stay of execution that would allow the two sides to iron out their differences.
The Commission, which has ruled the French scheme as it stands illegal, has already given France a stay of execution twice in the past month to allow it to come up with changes.

The Commission ordered Belgium last December to recover aid given indirectly to textiles exporters in the form of reduced social security contributions and warned Paris at the same time that its scheme could well meet the same fate.

The French aid had so far preserved 35,000 jobs, or half of those that would have been lost in an industry plunged into difficulty by cheaper imports from rivals in countries whose currencies had fallen against the franc, Barrot told reporters.
He said it was too early to put a price on the extension of the current scheme but said it would clearly be constrained by the need for a disciplined 1998 budget.
